channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102696: Critical: php:8.2 security update
item.description: An update for the php:8.2 module is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 Extended Update Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Critical. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Cybersecurity Jobs Open Now, November 24, 2026
item.description: A new Applied Cyber, Detections role is listed by Help Net Security, targeting remote positions in the United States. Candidates will support detection operations, develop and refine detection logic, and automate alert triage across web domains, social media, and other digital channels. The posting encourages collaboration with engineering and product teams to enhance detection capabilities and address evolving cyber threats.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102695: Critical: php:8.2 security update
item.description: An update for the php:8.2 module is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.4 Update Services for SAP Solutions. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Critical. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Update for RHEL 9.2 SAP
item.description: Red Hat issued a kernel update for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.2 Update Services for SAP Solutions, addressing multiple security bugs. The advisory rates the update as Important, with CVSS base scores linked to individual CVE references, indicating high risk if unpatched. Security teams should apply the update promptly, ensuring kernel version compliance and verifying SAP application compatibility after installation.

item.title: USN-9189-1: Qt5Compat vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that Qt5Compat did not correctly handle certain text codec names, which could lead to an out-of-bounds read. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102684: Critical: php:8.3 security update
item.description: An update for the php:8.3 module is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 Extended Update Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Critical. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Chrome 158 Released for Android
item.description: Google has released Chrome 158 (158.0.8127.92) for Android, which will appear on Google Play within days. The update focuses on stability and performance enhancements, while incorporating the same security fixes present in the corresponding desktop releases for Windows, Mac, and Linux. Users should install the new package via Google Play; no additional work-around is required.

item.title: Red Hat issues python-oauthlib security update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for python-oauthlib on RHEL 9, addressing multiple critical vulnerabilities. The update mitigates flaws that could enable remote code execution or privilege escalation, with CVSS scores linked via CVE references and rated Important by Product Security. Administrators should apply RHSA-2026:102668 immediately to secure affected systems.

item.title: Aurora stops ClickFix attacks with intent detection
item.description: ClickFix attacks coerce users into executing malicious commands, creating a gray zone that evades traditional security tools. Aurora Adaptive Threat Protection employs intent-based detection to recognize execution patterns, stopping attacks at the moment they occur and mapping activity for visibility. Security teams can integrate Aurora to gain real-time protection against ClickFix and similar command-execution threats.

item.title: OT Gateways Reveal Authentication Status, Many Unprotected
item.description: Industrial serial gateways reveal whether they are authenticated, exposing a flaw in critical OT access devices. The default configuration broadcasts authentication status, allowing attackers to identify unprotected devices; no exploit is needed, but the disclosure raises credential theft risk. Disable status broadcasts, enforce authentication, and apply vendor firmware updates that conceal authentication state.

item.title: 13 Malicious NuGet Packages Target .NET Developers
item.description: Socket researchers identified 13 malicious NuGet packages that lure .NET developers with fake job assessment prompts. The packages perform DLL side-loading, steal credentials, and embed GitHub-based malware, compromising developer environments. Security teams should audit package sources, enforce trusted feeds, and apply the latest .NET security updates to mitigate exposure and monitor for suspicious activity.

item.title: AWS SSM Agent default key flaw exposes role credentials
item.description: Amazon SSM Agent on AWS Windows Server AMIs contains a flaw where instances share a default cryptographic key during registration. CVE-2026-134069 allows a local non-admin user to retrieve the instance’s Default Host Management Configuration role credentials, enabling potential credential theft. AWS recommends updating to the latest SSM Agent version or applying the provided patch to eliminate the shared key vulnerability.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Golang Update for RHEL 10
item.description: Red Hat released a golang update for RHEL 10, fixing multiple security bugs in the Go compiler and runtime. The update addresses several CVE-linked issues, each with a CVSS base score indicating moderate impact; no active exploitation is known. Red Hat advises applying the update via the package manager; no workaround is needed.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Golang Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the golang runtime on RHEL 9, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update mitigates unspecified bugs that could allow local privilege escalation or code execution, with CVSS scores available via referenced CVE links. Administrators should apply the golang package update immediately to maintain system integrity.

item.title: CrowdStrike Acquires Zscaler for AI Security Integration
item.description: CrowdStrike announced a $44 billion acquisition of Zscaler, merging endpoint protection with zero-trust network security. The integration aims to centralize AI agent oversight, enabling unified threat detection across device and network layers. Customers will receive combined platform capabilities, but must plan for migration and potential licensing adjustments, ensuring seamless transition.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Python 3.6 Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the python36:3.6 module on RHEL 8, addressing several vulnerabilities. The patch fixes bugs that could enable local privilege escalation or arbitrary code execution, with CVSS scores provided via CVE references. System administrators should install the updated python36 package promptly to secure their environments.

item.title: Aurora ADTP Blocks Modern Attacks by Continuous Behavior Tracking
item.description: Aurora Adaptive Threat Protection (ADTP) monitors endpoint activity to counter attacks that bypass conventional defenses. By linking related behaviors into a full attack narrative, ADTP identifies malicious intent before execution, enabling real-time disruption. Security teams should deploy ADTP alongside existing endpoint solutions and configure behavior thresholds for optimal coverage, reducing blind spots.

item.title: KEPCO Breach Exposes 1.5 Million Customer Records
item.description: A threat actor breached KEPCO’s internal network, accessing two systems that stored customer, employee, and contractor data. The intrusion leveraged an undisclosed vulnerability in the company’s network perimeter, enabling unauthorized data exfiltration and potential credential compromise. KEPCO has issued a security advisory and is conducting a forensic investigation, urging affected users to monitor accounts and change passwords.

item.title: Chrome Stable Channel Updated to 158.0.8127.88
item.description: Google Chrome released a stable channel update to version 158.0.8127.88 for Windows, Mac, and Linux, rolling out over the next weeks. The update includes security fixes, with a detailed change log available; users are encouraged to review the log before upgrading. Administrators should schedule the rollout, verify compatibility, and monitor for any post-upgrade issues via the community help forum.

item.title: Chrome Extended Stable Channel Updated to 156.0.8078.114
item.description: Google Chrome’s Extended Stable channel updated to 156.0.8078.114 for Windows and macOS, extending the stable release schedule. The update lists changes, with security fixes pending a later release, and will roll out over the next days or weeks. Users may review the change log, file bugs, or use the community forum while awaiting the security patch.

item.title: CVE-2026-134056 - Out-of-bounds write in padded block cipher decryption in AWS-LC
item.description: Bulletin ID: 2026-196-AWS Publication Date: 11/23/2026 12:00 PM PST Description: We identified CVE-2026-134056, an out-of-bounds write issue in AWS-LC's padded block cipher decryption. If the output buffer is the minimum documented size, AWS-LC can write one byte past its end. The aws-lc-rs StreamingDecryptingKey API has a similar issue with cbc_pkcs7 and ecb_pkcs7.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Important SQLite Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released an important security update for SQLite on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update carries an Important impact rating, with CVSS base scores linked to each CVE in the advisory references. Administrators should apply the update immediately and verify that SQLite components are patched to mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: Cisco Products Affected by PHP Remote Code Vulnerability
item.description: Cisco products are vulnerable to a PHP flaw that permits remote code execution, as disclosed by the PHP Foundation on November 19, 2026. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-126714 and dubbed phpAfterShell, carries a Critical security impact rating and is referenced by GHSA-fm2m-fjf5-v3cp. Cisco recommends applying the available PHP security patches immediately to mitigate the RCE risk and ensure system integrity.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Moderate Update for go-toolset:rhel8
item.description: Red Hat released a moderate security update for the go-toolset:rhel8 module on RHEL8, fixing multiple Go compiler bugs. The patch addresses local privilege escalation and denial-of-service flaws with CVSS scores up to 7.5, though no active exploitation is known. Red Hat advises applying the update via the standard RHEL8 update channel; no workarounds are required.

item.title: Trump Names Industry Veteran Davies as Acting Cyber Director
item.description: Trump appointed Kirsten Davies as National Cyber Director, signaling a shift toward industry expertise amid outages and geopolitical tensions. The move follows criticism of cyber leadership and aims to leverage Davies' private sector experience to strengthen U.S. cyber defenses. The appointment is expected to influence policy direction and coordination with industry partners, though no immediate operational changes have been announced.

item.title: OpenRouter Removes AI Providers for Data Handling Violations
item.description: OpenRouter removed three AI providers after discovering they violated data-handling policies and exposed sensitive user prompts and secrets. The policy breach leaked proprietary prompts, potentially compromising client confidentiality and violating OpenRouter's privacy commitments. OpenRouter suspended the providers, issued a public notice, and is reviewing vetting procedures to prevent future violations.

item.title: Ubuntu OAuthLib multiple CVE vulnerabilities disclosed
item.description: Ubuntu 20.04 to 26.10 releases contain several OAuthLib flaws affecting token revocation, PKCE verification, and client identity validation. CVE-2026-49264 permits arbitrary code execution via JSONP callbacks, CVE-2026-49265 enables token theft through non-constant-time comparison, and CVE-2026-118669 allows unauthorized token acquisition by bypassing client checks. Users should upgrade to Ubuntu releases or apply the security patches to mitigate these OAuthLib vulnerabilities.

item.title: Chrome iOS Stable 158 Released with Stability Improvements
item.description: Google released Chrome Stable 158 (158.0.8127.86) for iOS, adding stability and performance improvements to the mobile browser. The update addresses minor bugs and optimizes rendering, reducing memory usage and enhancing page load times on iOS devices. The new build will be available on the App Store within hours, and users are encouraged to update to benefit from the fixes.

item.title: LaLiga Data Breach Exposes Fans Personal Information
item.description: LaLiga disclosed a breach that exposed personal data of its users and some affiliated clubs. The theft included names, email addresses, phone numbers, and other sensitive information, raising significant privacy and regulatory concerns. LaLiga notified affected users, launched incident response, and is cooperating with law enforcement to trace the attack.

item.title: MISP Advises Hotfix for Pre-v2.5.53 Vulnerabilities
item.description: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security issued advisory AV26-1197, noting that MISP versions prior to 2.5.53 contain multiple security vulnerabilities. A quick hotfix, version 2.5.53, addresses the identified flaws, and administrators are urged to review the provided links and apply updates as soon as possible. Failure to patch may leave MISP installations vulnerable to exploitation of the disclosed weaknesses.

item.title: AI Detects New Attacks by Learning Normal Behavior
item.description: Arctic Wolf's AI threat detection platform identifies new attacks by learning normal user, device, and system behavior. The system flags deviations that may indicate emerging threats, enabling security teams to investigate and respond to previously unseen attacks. This approach expands detection coverage beyond signature-based methods, improving overall security posture for organizations worldwide.

item.title: New Framework Traces Decade of Ransomware Actors
item.description: A new attribution framework enables security teams to trace ransomware actors across a decade of operations. The framework aggregates metadata from ransomware campaigns, correlating signatures and infrastructure to identify individual threat actors, thereby improving threat intelligence and response. Security teams can adopt the framework to enhance attribution accuracy, integrate with existing SIEMs, and prioritize defensive measures against identified actors.

item.title: Webworm Modifies SoftEther VPN to Evade Detection
item.description: The China-aligned threat actor Webworm is suspected of deploying a custom SoftEther VPN Bridge variant designed to conceal itself from security tools. The modified bridge removes recognizable detection fingerprints and masquerades as network-monitoring software, enabling covert remote access to compromised networks. Defenders should monitor anomalous VPN traffic, verify SoftEther installations against known hashes, and apply patches to mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: USN-9187-1: libssh vulnerabilities
item.description: This issue only affected Ubuntu 16.04 LTS, Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-59843) Mikhail Ilin and Saransh Rana discovered that libssh did not correctly sanitize shell metacharacters when expanding usernames in ProxyCommand strings. An attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive information. (CVE-2026-59846) Ben Smyth discovered that libssh incorrectly verified AES-GCM authentication tags when built with the OpenSSL backend.

item.title: CrowdStrike Acquires Zscaler for $43.9B
item.description: CrowdStrike announced the acquisition of Zscaler in a $43.9 billion deal, aiming to expand its AI-driven security portfolio. The purchase reflects CEO George Kurtz’s vision of building the largest AI safety and security company worldwide. The transaction is expected to integrate Zscaler’s cloud security platform with CrowdStrike’s endpoint protection, pending regulatory approval.

item.title: GlobeTopper Suffers Cyberattack Causing Financial and Operational Losses
item.description: B2B top-up solutions provider GlobeTopper suffered a cyberattack that disrupted its business operations and compromised digital assets. Attackers redeemed digital gift cards valued at $70,000, resulting in an estimated total operational revenue loss of $2.5 million for the company. Organizations should review digital asset transaction controls and implement strict access monitoring on top-up management systems.

item.title: China-Nexus Actor Exploits Medical Imaging Zero-Day via Cairn
item.description: A China-nexus threat actor targeted East Asian universities by deploying the Cairn penetration testing tool to execute attacks. The adversary exploited an unpatched zero-day vulnerability in a medical imaging application, escalating privileges from flaw discovery to root access within 11 minutes. Security teams must monitor for unauthorized Cairn execution and audit medical imaging software for unauthenticated access vectors.

item.title: Red Hat Issues freerdp Patch for RHEL 9
item.description: Red Hat released an important freerdp update for RHEL 9, addressing several security vulnerabilities. The flaws could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code or exfiltrate session data, yet no active exploitation has been reported. Security teams should apply the freerdp patch immediately, verify remote desktop configurations, and monitor for suspicious activity.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Important Netpbm Patch for RHEL 10
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the netpbm package affecting Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 installations. The underlying security flaws received an Important severity rating from Red Hat Product Security, with detailed base scores published in accompanying advisories. System administrators should apply the updated netpbm packages via standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux package management systems.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Netpbm Update for RHEL 9.8 EUS
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update addressing vulnerabilities in the netpbm package for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support. Red Hat Product Security categorized the security impact as Important, providing Common Vulnerability Scoring System base scores across referenced advisories. Administrators managing Extended Update Support environments must deploy the updated netpbm packages to mitigate potential security risks.

item.title: Microsoft Security Response Center acknowledges CVE-2026-69291
item.description: Microsoft Security Response Center acknowledges CVE-2026-69291, a remote code execution flaw in the Windows Volume Manager Extension Driver. The vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary code via crafted volume manager requests that can be triggered by malicious input, potentially compromising affected systems. A patch is available; administrators should apply the update promptly to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Microsoft Security Response Center acknowledges CVE-2026-87697
item.description: Microsoft Security Response Center acknowledges CVE-2026-87697, a remote code execution flaw in the .NET runtime. The vulnerability permits attackers to run arbitrary code through crafted .NET assemblies that can be triggered by malicious input, potentially compromising affected applications. A patch is available; developers should update .NET to the latest version to mitigate the risk.

item.title: ASP.NET Core Denial of Service CVE-2026-96233
item.description: A denial-of-service flaw in ASP.NET Core, CVE-2026-96233, lets attackers exhaust server resources via crafted HTTP requests. The flaw arises from improper input validation in request parsing, and no public exploit is known, but it can cause service interruption. Microsoft released a patch that corrects the parsing logic; administrators should apply the latest ASP.NET Core update or vendor hotfix.

item.title: Windows Message Queuing DoS CVE-2026-119848
item.description: CVE-2026-119848 is a denial-of-service flaw in Windows Message Queuing that lets attackers crash the service with malformed queue messages. The vulnerability stems from unchecked bounds during message deserialization, and no active exploitation is known, but it can cause repeated service restarts. Microsoft released a patch that validates message lengths; administrators should apply Windows update or vendor hotfix to mitigate DoS.

item.title: Microsoft Acknowledges CVE-2026-70175 ASP.NET Core Privilege Bug
item.description: Microsoft has acknowledged CVE-2026-70175, an elevation of privilege flaw in ASP.NET Core that could let attackers gain higher privileges on affected systems. The flaw stems from improper validation of user input during authentication, allowing privilege escalation without authentication, though no public exploit exists. Microsoft issued an update; users should watch for future patches and apply any subsequent fixes when available.

item.title: Microsoft Acknowledges CVE-2026-96225 .NET Privilege Bug
item.description: Microsoft has acknowledged CVE-2026-96225, an elevation of privilege flaw in .NET that could allow attackers to gain higher privileges on affected systems. The vulnerability arises from validation errors during authentication, enabling privilege escalation without authentication, though no public exploit has been reported. Microsoft issued an update; users should watch for future patches and apply any subsequent fixes when available.

item.title: Microsoft Acknowledges CVE-2026-78462 in VS Code
item.description: Microsoft acknowledges CVE-2026-78462, a Visual Studio Code security feature bypass vulnerability. The issue could allow attackers to bypass security controls, but no public exploit or PoC has been disclosed. Microsoft has issued an informational update; no patch or mitigation is required at this time, and the vulnerability is tracked in the Microsoft Security Advisory database.

item.title: Microsoft Acknowledges CVE-2026-72965 in Windows
item.description: Microsoft acknowledges CVE-2026-72965, a Windows WebClient Service elevation of privilege vulnerability. The flaw could allow local users to gain higher privileges, but no public exploit or PoC has been disclosed. Microsoft has issued an informational update; no patch or mitigation is required at this time, and the vulnerability is tracked in the Microsoft Security Advisory database.

item.title: Splunk Advisory Affects Multiple Products, Requires Upgrade
item.description: Splunk issued a security advisory (AV26-1196) affecting multiple products, including Enterprise, Enterprise Security, PCI Compliance, and SOAR, with versions prior to specified releases. The vulnerabilities could enable unauthorized access or privilege escalation within Splunk deployments, but no active exploitation has been confirmed. Administrators should review the provided links, upgrade to newer versions, and enforce access controls to mitigate risk.

item.title: Microsoft Patches Exploited Azure API Management Flaw Targeting Energy Sector Credentials
item.description: Microsoft patched an Azure API Management flaw that attackers exploited to target Norwegian energy companies and other sectors. The vulnerability let attackers read protected configuration data and credential vaults, potentially exposing API secrets and sensitive information. Microsoft urged affected customers to apply the update or configuration changes immediately to block unauthorized credential access.
